passages.scripture: My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you will not sin. But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate before the Father—Jesus Christ, the Righteous One.

lines.text: John's little children are the people who believe in Jesus, including us.
John writes these things to his little children.
John writes so that his little children will not sin.
But suppose anyone does sin.
Then we have an advocate before the Father.
The advocate is Jesus Christ.
Jesus Christ is the Righteous One.

passages.scripture: He Himself is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not only for ours but also for the sins of the whole world.

lines.text: Jesus Himself is the atoning sacrifice for our sins.
That is, Jesus sacrificed His life by dying to atone for our sins, paying the price for our forgiveness.
And Jesus is the atoning sacrifice not only for our sins.
But Jesus is also the atoning sacrifice for the sins of the whole world.

passages.scripture: Beloved, I am not writing to you a new commandment, but an old one, which you have had from the beginning. This commandment is the message you have heard.

lines.text: John writes to you, whom he loves.
John is not writing a new commandment.
Instead, John is writing an old commandment.
You have had this commandment from the beginning.
This old commandment is the message you have heard.

passages.scripture: By this we can be sure that we have come to know Him: if we keep His commandments.

lines.text: Suppose we keep God's commandments.
To keep God's commandments is to obey what God commands.
By this we can be sure that we have come to know God.

passages.scripture: If anyone says, “I know Him,” but does not keep His commandments, he is a liar, and the truth is not in him.

lines.text: Suppose we say that we know God.
But suppose we do not keep God's commandments.
Then we are liars.
And the truth is not in us.

passages.scripture: But if anyone keeps His word, the love of God has been truly perfected in him. By this we know that we are in Him: Whoever claims to abide in Him must walk as Jesus walked.

lines.text: But suppose anyone — any of us — keeps God's word.
Then God's love is truly perfected — made complete — in us.
Suppose anyone — any of us — claims to abide in God — to stay close to God.
Then we must walk as Jesus walked — we must live as Jesus lived.
If we walk as Jesus walked, then we know that we are in God — that we belong to God.

passages.scripture: Then again, I am also writing to you a new commandment, which is true in Him and also in you. For the darkness is fading and the true light is already shining.

lines.text: Then again, John also writes to you a new commandment.
This new commandment is true in God.
And this commandment is also true in you.
For the darkness — life apart from God — is fading.
And the true light — God's own light, which came through Jesus — is already shining.

passages.scripture: Whoever loves his brother remains in the light, and there is no cause of stumbling in him.

lines.text: Suppose anyone — any of us — loves their brothers and sisters in Jesus.
Then we remain in the light, with God.
And nothing in us makes us stumble and fall.

passages.scripture: If anyone claims to be in the light but hates his brother, he is still in the darkness.

lines.text: Suppose anyone — any of us — claims to be in the light, with God.
But suppose we hate one of our brothers or sisters — a fellow believer in Jesus.
Then we are still in the darkness, apart from God.

passages.scripture: But whoever hates his brother is in the darkness and walks in the darkness. He does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes.

lines.text: We should never hate one of our brothers or sisters.
If we hate, then we are in the darkness, apart from God.
If we hate, then we also walk in the darkness.
If we hate, then the darkness has blinded our eyes — now we cannot see.
If we hate, then because we are blind, we do not know where we are going.

passages.scripture: I am writing to you, little children, because your sins have been forgiven through His name.

lines.text: John writes to you, little children — God's dear children.
John writes because your sins have been forgiven.
This forgiveness is through the name of Jesus — because of what He has done.

passages.scripture: I am writing to you, fathers, because you know Him who is from the beginning. I am writing to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one. I have written to you, children, because you know the Father.

lines.text: John writes to you, fathers — you who are mature in the faith.
You fathers know God, who has been from the beginning.
John also writes to you, young men — you who are strong in the faith.
You young men have overcome the evil one — the devil.
John has written to you, children — you who are young in the faith.
You children know the Father — God.

passages.scripture: I have written to you, fathers, because you know Him who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God abides in you, and you have overcome the evil one.

lines.text: John has written to you, fathers — you who are mature in the faith.
You fathers know God, who has been from the beginning.
John has also written to you, young men — you who are strong in the faith.
You young men are strong.
And the word of God lives in you young men.
And you young men have overcome the evil one — the devil.

passages.scripture: Do not love the world or anything in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him.

lines.text: Do not love the world — the way of life turned away from God.
Do not love anything in the world.
If anyone — any of us — loves the world, then we do not love God the Father.

passages.scripture: For all that is in the world—the desires of the flesh, the desires of the eyes, and the pride of life—is not from the Father but from the world.

lines.text: Here is why: everything in the world — the way of life turned away from God — is not from God the Father.
In the world are the desires of the flesh — the cravings of our sinful nature.
In the world are the desires of the eyes — greedily wanting whatever we see.
And in the world is the pride of life — boasting about what we have and who we are.
None of it comes from God the Father — it all comes from the world.

passages.scripture: The world is passing away, along with its desires; but whoever does the will of God remains forever.

lines.text: The world is passing away — the way of life turned away from God will not last.
The world's desires are passing away too — its cravings will not last.
But anyone — any of us — who does what God wants lives forever.

passages.scripture: Children, it is the last hour; and just as you have heard that the antichrist is coming, so now many antichrists have appeared. This is how we know it is the last hour.

lines.text: Dear children, it is the last hour — the final age before Jesus comes back.
Just as you have heard that the antichrist is coming — the one who stands against Christ — so now many antichrists have appeared.
This is how we know it is the last hour — the final age.

passages.scripture: They went out from us, but they did not belong to us. For if they had belonged to us, they would have remained with us. But their departure made it clear that none of them belonged to us.

lines.text: These antichrists went out from us — they left the true believers.
But they — these antichrists — never truly belonged to us.
For if these antichrists had truly belonged to us, they would have stayed with us.
But their leaving made it clear: not one of these antichrists ever belonged to us.

passages.scripture: You, however, have an anointing from the Holy One, and all of you know the truth.

lines.text: But you have an anointing from the Holy One — God's Holy Spirit, given to you.
And all of you know the truth — the true teaching about Jesus.

passages.scripture: I have not written to you because you lack knowledge of the truth, but because you have it, and because no lie comes from the truth.

lines.text: John did not write to you because you do not know the truth — but because you already know it.
And John wrote because no lie ever comes from the truth.

passages.scripture: Who is the liar, if it is not the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the antichrist, who denies the Father and the Son.

lines.text: Who is the liar? It is none other than the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ — God's promised Savior and King.
This person is the antichrist: the one who denies both the Father, who is God, and the Son, who is Jesus.

passages.scripture: Whoever denies the Son does not have the Father, but whoever confesses the Son has the Father as well.

lines.text: Anyone who denies the Son, Jesus, does not have the Father, God.
But anyone — any of us — who openly confesses the Son, Jesus, has the Father, God, too.

passages.scripture: As for you, let what you have heard from the beginning remain in you. If it does, you will also remain in the Son and in the Father.

lines.text: As for you, let the message you heard from the beginning — the first good news about Jesus — remain in you.
If that message remains in you, then you too will remain joined to the Son, Jesus, and to the Father, God.

passages.scripture: And this is the promise that He Himself made to us: eternal life.

lines.text: And God Himself made a promise to us.
That promise is eternal life — life forever with God.

passages.scripture: I have written these things to you about those who are trying to deceive you.

lines.text: John has written these things to you.
John wrote these things about those who are trying to deceive you — to pull you away from the truth.

passages.scripture: And as for you, the anointing you received from Him remains in you, and you do not need anyone to teach you. But just as His true and genuine anointing teaches you about all things, so remain in Him as you have been taught.

lines.text: As for you, you received the anointing from God — His Holy Spirit.
And that anointing remains in you.
And you do not need anyone to teach you — you already have the truth.
God's anointing is true.
And God's anointing is genuine.
God's anointing teaches you about everything.
And God's anointing has taught you all along.
So remain in God.

passages.scripture: And now, little children, remain in Christ, so that when He appears, we may be confident and unashamed before Him at His coming.

lines.text: And now, dear children, remain in Christ — stay joined to Jesus.
So when Jesus appears, we can stand confident.
And we will not be ashamed before Jesus when He comes back.

passages.scripture: If you know that He is righteous, you also know that everyone who practices righteousness has been born of Him.

lines.text: You know that God is righteous — He always does what is right.
So you also know that anyone — any of us — who does what is right has been born of God — made His child.
